correctness.rationale: All unordered edge-type pairs are exhausted by the explicit distance formulas for matching and horizontal edges. Matching-edge separation forces at most one empty matched column, proving size at least n-1; the collision conditions then prove n-1 feasibility exactly for n>=7 with both layers represented at least three times. At size n the only occupancy types are full transversals or one hole plus one doubled column, and pairwise criteria classify every valid instance including n=2. Exact disjoint counting follows. The standalone Python BFS checker independently enumerated every candidate at the alleged minimum size through n=11, checking actual edge-distance vectors and distance-one edge domination, with all counts agreeing. No extrapolation from finite checks is used.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Complete prism means K_n Cartesian K_2 (two K_n layers with a matching). Vertex-edge dominant edge metric requires resolving edge pairs and distance-one vertex-edge domination; it is not mixed metric dimension or edge-version metric dimension using line-graph distances. The paper of 2022 defines precisely the studied invariant. The closest prism alias in older edge-version literature is C_n Cartesian K_2 (a cycle prism), a distinct family.

originality.rationale: Examined the defining 2022 manuscript and the relevant product section of the full 2024 publication as accessible HTML full text. The 2022 work gives the invariant and Cartesian path/cycle families; the 2024 product theorem yields only the interval n-1 through n on K_n square K_2, not the order-seven threshold or exact bases. Indexed complete-prism mixed-metric results concern a stronger distinct resolving problem, whose minima are n from n>=5. value.rationale: This gives the sharp endpoint selection in the prior [n-1,n] prism inequality and every minimum basis, including a genuine sharp transition at n=7 and explicit exponential multiplicities. It directly resolves a natural Cartesian graph family for the purpose of edge landmark placement; the distinction from mixed metric bases is structural, not an arbitrary numeric slice. The theorem has a uniform proof and includes low-order exceptional configurations.
